questions.q:
With reference to the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), consider the following statements:
1. It is built on the Immediate Payment Service (IMPS) infrastructure.
2. It was developed by the Reserve Bank of India and is operated by it directly.
3. In 2026, Greece and the Maldives began accepting UPI.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. UPI was developed by the National Payments Corporation of India, an RBI-regulated entity, not by the RBI itself. UPI is now accepted in 11 countries: Greece through Eurobank, the Maldives through its Favara system and Cambodia through ACLEDA Bank, along with Bhutan, Nepal, Singapore, the UAE, France, Sri Lanka, Mauritius and Qatar.

questions.q:
Arrange the following UPI milestones in chronological order:
1. Launch of the BHIM app
2. UPI crossing 1 billion monthly transactions
3. Launch of UPI Circle for delegated payments
4. Introduction of on-device biometric authentication
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: BHIM came in December 2016, UPI crossed a billion monthly transactions in October 2019, UPI Circle came in 2024, and fingerprint or face authentication and Aadhaar face authentication for PIN set-up came in 2025. UPI handled about 49 per cent of the world's real-time payments in 2024.

questions.q:
With reference to the FAO Food Price Index, consider the following statements:
1. It is published every quarter.
2. Its base is the 2002-2004 average.
3. It is a weighted average of price indices for seven commodity groups, including fertilisers and fuel.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None of the statements is correct. The index is monthly, its base is the 2014-2016 average (the 2002-2004 base was used earlier), and it averages five groups: cereals, vegetable oils, dairy, meat and sugar, across 24 items. It reached a three-and-a-half-year high in July 2026 on heatwaves, El Nino and attacks on Black Sea ports.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Report : Subject
1. SOFO : State of the World's Forests
2. SOFIA : State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture
3. SOCO : State of Agricultural Commodity Markets
4. SOFI : State of Food and Agriculture
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. SOFI is The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World. All four are FAO flagship reports. The FAO has 195 members, 194 countries and the EU, and publishes the monthly Food Price Index.

questions.q: The Kerch Strait, mentioned in the context of disruptions to grain shipments in 2026, connects
o: the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara
the Caspian Sea and the Sea of Azov
the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov
the Sea of Marmara and the Aegean Sea
questions.e: The Kerch Strait lies between Crimea and Russia's Krasnodar region. Attacks on Black Sea ports and ships, including Novorossiysk in Russia and Izmail, a Ukrainian Danube port, raised insurance costs and threatened wheat, maize and sunflower-oil routes. The Bosporus links the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara (static GK).

questions.q:
With reference to Urban Co-operative Banks (UCBs), consider the following statements:
1. The first urban co-operative credit society was registered at Kanjivaram in 1904.
2. They are regulated only by the Registrar of Co-operative Societies.
3. The RBI has issued new UCB licences every year since 2003.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. UCBs face dual regulation: the RBI governs banking functions under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, while the Registrar handles registration, audit and elections. The RBI resumed licensing in 2026 after more than two decades, with norms such as Rs 300 crore capital. UCBs peaked at 2,104 in 2003 and are now about 1,500.

questions.q: Under the RBI's proposed norms for new Urban Co-operative Bank licences, which one of the following is not a requirement?
o: Registration under the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act only
Net NPA of not more than 3 per cent
Capital adequacy ratio of at least 12 per cent
questions.e: There is no requirement to register only as a multi-State society; single-State UCBs register under State laws. The norms also expect about 10 years of operation and five years of sound finances. The aim is a small group of strong, well-governed banks, building on the four-tier framework of 2022.

questions.q:
With reference to India and gold in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. According to the World Gold Council, India was the largest gold jewellery market in the quarter, with about 27 per cent of global demand.
2. The RBI holds about 880 tonnes of official gold reserves.
3. The RBI has been raising its holdings of US Treasury securities while reducing gold.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The RBI has reduced reliance on US Treasuries while raising gold, so statement 3 reverses the trend. Gold hedges inflation and currency swings, reduces dependence on the dollar and insulates against sanctions; it also helped in the 1991 balance-of-payments crisis.

questions.q: The Monetary Policy Framework Agreement, which made the RBI responsible for inflation targeting, was signed between the Government and the RBI in
questions.e: The agreement was signed on 20 February 2015; the RBI Act, 1934 was later amended to give the MPC statutory backing. If the target is missed, the RBI must formally explain to the government. Other tools besides the repo rate are the CRR, the SLR and open market operations.

questions.q:
With reference to the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. A new Section 9D bars States from levying taxes on mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands except as prescribed by the Centre.
2. Levies already collected by States before the law came into force are not refundable.
3. Minor minerals such as sand and granite remain under State control.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three statements are correct. Uncollected past levies become invalid, and about 50 minor minerals stay with the States. States imposed about 14 levies, including land taxes of up to 20 per cent. As static GK, regulating mines is in Entry 54 of the Union List, while taxes on mineral rights are in Entry 50 of the State List, subject to limits set by Parliament.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Ethanol diversion was only a secondary cause of the sugar price surge of 2026.
Statement-II: The shortfall in sugar production against the first estimate exceeded the amount of sugar diverted to ethanol.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the first. About 30 lakh tonnes went to ethanol, but output fell about 34.5 lakh tonnes below the first projection, owing to excess rain in late 2025, red rot and top shoot borer in UP. Grain supplied about 68 per cent of ethanol to oil companies between November 2025 and July 2026.

questions.q: The sugarcane variety Co-0238, mentioned in the context of falling sugar output in Uttar Pradesh in 2026, has become increasingly vulnerable to
questions.e: Co-0238 is widely grown in UP and has become vulnerable to red rot, a fungal disease, and to the top shoot borer. Together with waterlogging from excess rain in September and October 2025, these cut sucrose accumulation and mill recovery. The government banned sugar exports until 30 September 2026 and allowed duty-free import of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar.

questions.q:
With reference to India's sugar sector, consider the following statements:
1. The Fair and Remunerative Price of sugarcane for 2026-27 is Rs 365 per quintal, fixed by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices.
2. Sugarcane now supplies about three-fourths of India's fuel ethanol.
3. The share of sugar diverted to ethanol has fallen since 2022-23.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 3 is correct. The FRP of Rs 365 per quintal at 10.25 per cent recovery is fixed by the Centre on the CACP's recommendation; the CACP only recommends (static GK). About three-fourths of ethanol now comes from grains, mainly maize, and sugar diversion fell from about 12 per cent in 2022-23 to about 9 per cent in 2025-26.

questions.q:
With reference to the National Food Security Act, 2013, consider the following statements:
1. Its beneficiary ceiling is still based on Census 2011.
2. Its effective coverage has fallen below 60 per cent of the estimated population.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. The ceiling of 81.35 crore rests on Census 2011, and with an estimated population of 146.4 crore in 2025 effective coverage is about 55.6 per cent, against the Act's design of 75 per cent rural and 50 per cent urban. Commentators want coverage updated after Census 2027.

questions.q: According to the ICMR-NIN dietary guidelines of 2024 cited in the debate on the PDS, cereals and millets should provide
o: at least 70 per cent of dietary energy
at most 25 per cent of dietary energy
at most 45 per cent of dietary energy
questions.e: The rest should come from pulses, beans, milk, nuts, vegetables, fruits and other protein foods. Commentators argue for financing diversification of the PDS basket without cutting cereal entitlements. NFHS-6 shows stunting at 29.3 per cent and only about 15 per cent of children aged 6-23 months with a minimally adequate diet.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Initiative : Purpose
1. PMGDISHA : Digital literacy for rural households
2. Womaniya : Onboarding women-owned enterprises on the Government e-Marketplace
3. Mahila E-Haat : Online marketplace for women entrepreneurs and SHGs
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. These are among the steps listed for gendered digital equity, which goes beyond access to ownership, digital literacy, financial autonomy, agency and empowerment. NFHS-6 shows women's internet use rising from 33.3 to 64.3 per cent, still well behind men at 80.5 per cent.

questions.q:
With reference to India's LPG supply in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. India is the world's largest consumer of LPG.
2. About one-third of India's LPG now comes from the United States.
3. LPG is mainly a mixture of methane and ethane.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None of the statements is correct. India is the second-largest LPG consumer after China; the petroleum minister said 67 per cent of its LPG now comes from the US; and LPG is mainly propane and butane, while natural gas is mostly methane. Imports from West Asia fell by almost 85 per cent between February and June 2026 amid the Hormuz crisis.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: US LPG often looks cheaper at source but less competitive when landed in India.
Statement-II: Voyages of US cargoes to India are much longer than those from West Asia.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the first: shipping costs over 25 to 35 days erode the price advantage. US LPG currently looks competitive only because Gulf prices carry a risk premium. Over-reliance on one supplier risks energy being used as a bargaining chip, and a strong dollar raises the rupee cost of each cargo.

questions.q:
With reference to Geographical Indications in India, consider the following statements:
1. More than 800 GI products are registered.
2. The GI Registry, with all-India jurisdiction, is located at Chennai.
3. The target is 10,000 GI registrations by 2030.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three statements are correct. Registration is valid for ten years and renewable, and about 607 GIs have been granted since 2014. Under Section 27 of the GI Act, 1999, any aggrieved person may seek cancellation. New Zealand will allow registration of Indian GIs such as Darjeeling Tea and Basmati Rice.

questions.q:
Which of the following are registered as GIs under the 'natural goods' category?
1. Makrana Marble
2. Panna Diamond
3. Kannauj Perfume
4. Lac of Purulia
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The five natural goods GIs are Makrana Marble, Chunar Balua Patthar, Lac of Purulia, Panna Diamond and Ambaji White Marble. Kannauj Perfume, like Nashik Valley Wine, is a manufactured GI. Examples of food GIs are Bardhaman Mihidana, Kendrapara Rasabali and Tirupathi Laddu.

questions.q: A 'Goldilocks economy' is best described as one with
o: sustained growth with low inflation, neither overheating nor slowing sharply
questions.e: Commentators said India's economy stayed in a Goldilocks zone despite the West Asia war: growth of 7 to 7.5 per cent expected in Q1 FY27, inflation near 4 per cent and a current account deficit of about 0.3 per cent of GDP. Reasons include 125 basis points of repo cuts between December 2024 and December 2025, GST rationalisation, services exports and remittances.

questions.q:
With reference to the risks to India's economy discussed in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Goods inflation was running below services inflation.
2. Services make up about one-third of the CPI basket.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Goods inflation was about 5.4 per cent and services about 2.5 per cent, so goods were higher. Since services weigh about 33 per cent in the CPI, a rise in services inflation could lift the headline and force the RBI to tighten. Other risks are AI disruption of IT exports, El Nino and a reversal of manufacturing front-loading.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not among the six principles of regenerative agriculture listed in 2026?
o: Maximise use of synthetic fertilisers to raise yields
questions.e: The six principles are minimising soil disturbance, maintaining soil cover, limiting chemical inputs, keeping living roots of perennial crops, integrating livestock and enhancing biodiversity. Agriculture grew at 4.45 per cent over FY16 to FY25. Supporting schemes include the National Mission on Natural Farming, PKVY, Per Drop More Crop and the Soil Health Card.

questions.q:
Which of the following are on-farm bio-inputs used in natural farming?
1. Jeevamrut
2. Beejamrut
3. Neemastra
4. Dashparni
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: All four are natural-farming inputs prepared from native livestock dung and urine and local plants, along with Ghanjeevamrut: Beejamrut treats seeds, Jeevamrut and Ghanjeevamrut enrich soil microbes, and Neemastra and Dashparni are botanical pest repellents. Natural farming also uses traditional seeds, mulching, minimal tillage and multi-cropping.

questions.q:
With reference to India's power capacity in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Non-fossil capacity crossed 300 GW, more than half of total installed capacity.
2. Wind is the largest source of non-fossil capacity.
3. A record 85 GW of non-fossil capacity was added in 2025-26.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Solar, at about 165 GW, is by far the largest non-fossil source, followed by wind at about 58 GW and hydro at about 57 GW. The record addition in 2025-26 was 55.29 GW. Non-fossil capacity is now 60 per cent of the 500 GW target for 2030.

questions.q:
Which of the following are among the five most abundant greenhouse gases?
1. Water vapour
2. Ozone
3. Nitrous oxide
4. Sulphur dioxide
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The five most abundant greenhouse gases are water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and ozone; synthetic gases such as CFCs and HCFCs also trap heat. Sulphur dioxide is an air pollutant that forms cooling aerosols, not a greenhouse gas. Greenhouse gas emission intensity means emissions per unit of output.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Storage technology : Principle
1. Pumped hydro : Surplus power pumps water uphill for later release through turbines
2. Concentrating solar-thermal : Molten salt stores heat to raise steam later
3. Flywheel : Stores energy as rotational motion for near-instant injection
4. Gravity storage : Compressed air is stored in underground caverns
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Gravity storage lifts heavy weights and regenerates power by lowering them; storing compressed air in caverns is compressed-air storage. Lithium-ion batteries, especially lithium iron phosphate, dominate grid-scale battery storage.

questions.q:
With reference to the Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana, consider the following statements:
1. It targets 5,000 MW of floating solar capacity with co-located storage of at least two hours.
2. It is implemented by NTPC as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
3. It offers central financial assistance of Rs 1 crore per MW on commissioning.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. It is a Central Sector Scheme of MNRE implemented by the Solar Energy Corporation of India, with Rs 5,070 crore for FY27 to FY31. It also offers up to Rs 50 lakh per site for feasibility studies. NISE puts India's floating-solar potential at about 102 GWp, against about 0.7 GW installed.

questions.q: Which State has the largest floating-solar potential according to the National Institute of Solar Energy, as cited for the PM Surya Sarovar Yojana?
questions.e: Maharashtra leads with about 16.28 GWp, followed by Madhya Pradesh with about 14.89 GWp, then Karnataka, Odisha, Telangana and Gujarat. Several of these are not traditional renewable leaders, so floating solar can decentralise solar generation. Floating projects already include Ramagundam (100 MW), Kayamkulam (92 MW) and Omkareshwar.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Floating solar panels can be more efficient than identical ground-mounted panels.
Statement-II: Solar cell efficiency rises as panel temperature rises.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect. PV efficiency falls with heat, so water cooling helps floating panels. Floating plants also shade water, cutting evaporation and algae, but cost about 25 per cent more than ground-mounted plants and suffer wear from waves and moisture.

questions.q:
With reference to India's energy transition, consider the following statements:
1. Coal now generates less than half of India's electricity.
2. Coal-bearing States such as Odisha and Jharkhand hold most of India's solar manufacturing capacity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither statement is correct. Coal still generates over 70 per cent of electricity despite its falling share of capacity. RE-rich States have about 78 per cent of solar PV manufacturing, while coal States (Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh) hold 87 per cent of coal reserves and get 75 per cent of mining royalties.

questions.q:
With reference to E20 petrol, consider the following statements:
1. Direct imports of ethanol for blending are banned.
2. Vehicles built after April 2020 under BS-6 Phase 1 norms are engineered for E20.
3. India's Ethanol Supply Year runs from April to March.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Vehicles engineered for E20 are those built after April 2023 under BS-6 Phase 2 (Real Driving Emissions) norms, about 23 per cent of the petrol fleet. The Ethanol Supply Year runs from November to October. India has 18 to 20 billion litres of ethanol capacity from about 500 distilleries.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: E20 can damage fuel systems in older vehicles that were not designed for it.
Statement-II: Ethanol is a polar solvent and is hygroscopic.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the first: as a solvent, ethanol hardens or cracks old rubber and plastics, and by absorbing water it can separate into an acidic layer in parked vehicles. Surveys report mileage losses, while IIT Kanpur found efficiency losses under 5 per cent. E85, by contrast, is meant only for flex-fuel vehicles.

questions.q:
With reference to the GOBARdhan National Circular Bioenergy Scheme approved in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Its nodal ministry is the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
2. City gas distribution entities must meet a compressed biogas obligation of 10 per cent from 2026-27.
3. It provides an administered price for compressed biogas of Rs 1,000 per MMBTU.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None of the statements is correct. The new scheme for FY27 to FY36 is run by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas; GOBARdhan began in 2018 under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen). The CBG obligation is 3 per cent in 2026-27, 4 per cent in 2027-28 and 5 per cent from 2028-29, and the administered price is Rs 2,110 per MMBTU, about Rs 105 per kg.

questions.q:
With reference to India's solar sector, consider the following statements:
1. India added more solar capacity than the United States in calendar year 2025.
2. The record low solar tariff of Rs 2.44 per unit was discovered at the Pavagada Solar Park.
3. The Approved List of Models and Manufacturers restricts government-backed projects to listed modules and cells.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Rs 2.44 tariff came at a Bhadla auction in Rajasthan in 2017, so statement 2 is wrong. India added 37 GW in 2025 and 44.61 GW in FY26, has 172 GW of module manufacturing capacity, and is the world's second-largest solar growth market.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Scheme : Feature
1. PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana : Domestic rooftop solar, launched in 2024
2. PM-KUSUM : Solar pumps and solarisation of agricultural feeders, launched in 2019
3. Green Energy Corridor : Production-linked incentives for solar modules
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. The Green Energy Corridor builds transmission to evacuate renewable power; it had evacuated about 24.6 GW by February 2026. Production-linked incentives for high-efficiency modules were approved in 2021 and expanded in 2022. Distributed solar made up about 36 per cent of FY26 additions.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Solar park : State
1. Bhadla : Rajasthan
2. Pavagada : Karnataka
3. Rewa : Madhya Pradesh
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. The Solar Parks Scheme, launched in 2014 with a 20 GW target raised to 40 GW in 2017, had sanctioned 54 parks by February 2026. The record low tariff of Rs 2.44 per unit came at a Bhadla auction in 2017, and Rewa is cited as a model for cutting costs and mobilising investment.

questions.q:
With reference to the Samudra Manthan National Offshore Exploration Scheme, consider the following statements:
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
2. It aims to develop additional reserves of 600 million tonnes of oil equivalent.
3. It supports drilling of 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three statements are correct. Phase-I has Rs 84,084 crore up to FY31 and covers up to half the drilling cost or Rs 675 crore per well, whichever is lower. India has begun its first appraisal well in the Mahanadi offshore basin. India is the third-largest crude consumer and spends about 144 billion dollars a year on crude imports.

questions.q:
With reference to India's strategic fuel reserves, consider the following statements:
1. Phase-I strategic petroleum reserves are at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur.
2. India has commercial underground storage for natural gas in depleted reservoirs.
3. LNG must be stored at about minus 162 degrees Celsius.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. India has no underground gas storage; LNG sits only in operational tanks at terminals, and depleted reservoirs or salt caverns are unproven commercially here. Phase-I SPR capacity is 5.33 MT and Phase-II adds 6.5 MT at Chandikhol and Padur. A proposed programme would add about 28 MT crude, 9 MT LNG and 4 MT LPG.

questions.q:
With reference to nuclear power in India, consider the following statements:
1. India's nuclear power generation began at Kalpakkam in 1969.
2. Indian PHWRs use enriched uranium with light water as moderator.
3. Thorium-232 is a fertile material that is converted into fissile uranium-233 in a reactor.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 3 is correct. Nuclear power generation began at Tarapur in 1969. Indian PHWRs use natural uranium with heavy water as moderator and coolant, avoiding enrichment. India has 24 reactors at 7 sites with 8.78 GW and a target of 100 GW by 2047. Thorium is found in coastal sands of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Reactor : Feature
1. BSMR-200 : 220 MWe Bharat Small Modular Reactor
2. SMR-55 : 55 MWe small modular reactor
3. High-Temperature Gas-Cooled Reactor : Intended for hydrogen production
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. Small modular reactors are generally up to 300 MWe, built in factories for faster construction; uses include remote areas, replacing retiring coal plants, process heat and hydrogen. The Nuclear Energy Mission in the 2025-26 Budget provides Rs 20,000 crore for indigenous SMRs.

questions.q:
With reference to radiation safety in India, consider the following statements:
1. The public dose limit from planned exposure is 1 millisievert per year, excluding natural background and medical exposure.
2. High-level nuclear waste is vitrified in a glass matrix.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. India follows a closed fuel cycle, reprocessing spent fuel, and uses the ALARA principle under AERB oversight. Indian PHWRs have two independent and diverse shutdown systems as part of defence-in-depth. Safety reviews after Fukushima in 2011 led to upgrades in backup power, cooling and external-hazard protection.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor at Kalpakkam marks the start of the second stage of India's nuclear programme.
Statement-II: The PFBR runs on natural uranium fuel with heavy water as coolant.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect. The PFBR, which reached first criticality in April 2026, uses plutonium-based MOX fuel and is led by IGCAR, with about 90 per cent of its equipment made in India. Natural uranium with heavy water is the first stage, the PHWRs; the third stage will use thorium.

questions.q:
With reference to the government's 2026 statement on the ethanol blending programme, consider the following statements:
1. It has saved about Rs 2 lakh crore in foreign exchange.
2. Oil companies buy ethanol at a price higher than the pump price of petrol.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct; the programme also substituted about 32 million tonnes of crude. OMCs buy ethanol at about Rs 70 a litre against a pump price of about Rs 105, but petrol's base price is only 55 to 60 per cent of the pump price, so ethanol is not clearly cheaper. During the West Asia war crude rose about 70 per cent but pump petrol only 7 to 8 per cent.

questions.q: With reference to the care economy, which one of the following statements is not correct?
o: It covers both paid and unpaid care work.
It includes care delivered by households and non-profits.
It concerns only childcare and excludes eldercare.
Investment in care can raise women's labour force participation.
questions.e: The care economy covers care across life stages: children, youth, adults, older persons, persons with disabilities and caregivers themselves. The AVPN Global Conference in New Delhi drew attention to impact investment in care. Urbanisation, nuclear families and ageing make care infrastructure central to women's employment and growth.

questions.q:
With reference to UPI features, consider the following statements:
1. UPI 123PAY allows payments from feature phones.
2. UPI Lite allows PIN-less low-value payments.
3. UPI Circle lets a primary user authorise secondary users within limits.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three statements are correct. UPI 123PAY works through IVR, missed calls and proximity sound, with a Rs 10,000 per-transaction limit; the UPI Lite wallet holds up to Rs 5,000, with Rs 1,000 per transaction. In 2024 the RBI also raised the UPI limit for tax payments to Rs 5 lakh.

questions.q: With reference to India's measures to cool food prices, the Open Market Sales Scheme involves
o: duty cuts on crude edible oils
release of government wheat and rice stocks into the open market
questions.e: Under OMSS the government sells wheat and rice from its stocks to cool wholesale prices. Other measures include export bans or minimum export prices on wheat, non-basmati rice and sugar, cuts in edible-oil import duties and stock limits on traders. Commentators want a shift from reactive controls to resilient food systems.

questions.q: Under the anti-hoarding measures for sugar announced in 2026, which one of the following is not correct?
o: Dealers may hold at most 400 tonnes of sugar.
Sugar exports were prohibited until 30 September 2026.
Mills were advised to start crushing from 15 October 2026.
Bulk consumers were exempted from any stock limit.
questions.e: From 1 September 2026, bulk consumers could hold at most 15 days of consumption, and mills had to report buyers taking 500 tonnes or more a year. Joint Centre-State teams verified mill stocks. Early crushing was meant to raise October output from the usual 3-4 lakh tonnes to over 10 lakh tonnes for the festive season.

questions.q:
With reference to India's LPG consumers in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. India had more than 30 crore active domestic LPG connections.
2. Beneficiaries of PM Ujjwala Yojana numbered more than 10 crore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct; there were about 33.14 crore active connections and 10.57 crore PMUY beneficiaries in July 2026. India produces about 40 per cent of its LPG and imports about 60 per cent. Shortages of cooking gas are politically sensitive, so availability takes priority over cost optimisation.

questions.q: 'PM Ekta Mall', mentioned in the context of promoting GI products, refers to
o: malls in States to promote One District One Product, GI products and handicrafts
an online marketplace run by GeM
railway stalls under One Station One Product
questions.e: PM Ekta Malls were given Rs 5,000 crore in 2023-24 to showcase ODOP, GI and handicraft products. One Station One Product stalls sell GI goods at railway stations, and Assam launched a Muga Silk Trail in June 2026. GI tags are said to raise rural artisans' incomes by 20 to 30 per cent.

questions.q: In 2026 India began drilling its first appraisal well in which offshore basin under a four-well deepwater programme?
questions.e: The appraisal well MN-DWN18-1-HD is in the Mahanadi offshore basin. Samudra Manthan aims to raise domestic output from about 62 to 80 million tonnes of oil equivalent a year and save about Rs 1 lakh crore annually.
